content:
customer_acme_inc: Hey team — since switching to the rwd-owl-64k variant we've started getting intermittent 429s. Happens across EU and US regions. Example response from our app: {
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "message": "per-model RPM/TPM limit exceeded"
  }
}

jess_support: Thanks for reporting — can you paste a minimal request (no API key) and say whether you're streaming and approx requests/min and parallelism?

customer_acme_inc: We're non-streaming. Typical pattern: we fan-out 12 parallel requests per user session, each request includes ~15k input tokens (lots of doc context) + asking for 1.5k tokens output. Total ~16.5k tokens/request. Traffic ~300 requests/min to that model (spikey, bursts up to 450rpm for ~30s).

ash_sre: That combination is heavyweight. A few things to call out:
- Our platform enforces per-model RPM and per-model TPM (tokens per minute) per account. Long-context variants consume a lot of TPM credit.
- There's also a max concurrent request cap per account per model (shared tier default is 10).
- Short bursts can be tolerated, but sustained or simultaneous spikes will trigger 429s with type rate_limit_exceeded or concurrency_limit_exceeded.

kevin_prod: To be concrete: for rwd-owl-64k currently the baseline limits for shared/hosted customers are around 400 RPM, ~120k TPM, and max concurrency 10. Those numbers vary by customer profile; the 64k variant has a lower TPM because token processing costs scale roughly O(n) with sequence length. If your avg tokens/request is 16.5k and you do 300 RPM that's ~4.95M tokens/min -> whoops math check: actually tokens/min = 16.5k * 300 = 4,950,000 tokens/min which far exceeds per-account TPM caps (we report TPM in hundreds of thousands), so you'll hit TPM throttles immediately. The 120k TPM is per minute, not per-request.

jess_support: Quick repro path we usually ask customers to run so we can correlate logs:
1) Run a single minimal curl against the model that reproduces the request body (no API key).
2) Repeat at several concurrencies (1, 4, 8, 12) and measure when 429s start.
3) Capture response headers (we include X-RateLimit-*, X-Model-Quota if available).

Example curl (remove real key when sharing):
```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=rwd-owl-64k' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input":"<very long doc...>","max_tokens":1500}'
```

customer_acme_inc: here's a dev log snippet we captured when the error happened: 
```json
{
  "status": 429,
  "error": {
    "type": "rate_limit_exceeded",
    "detail": "per_account_per_model_tpm",
    "retry_after": 27
  },
  "headers": {
    "x-ratelimit-limit-rpm": "400",
    "x-ratelimit-remaining-rpm": "0",
    "x-ratelimit-limit-tpm": "120000",
    "x-ratelimit-remaining-tpm": "-"
  }
}
```

ash_sre: That header set lines up with a TPM exhaustion. Two immediate mitigations to try: reduce concurrency (from 12 -> 4), and reduce per-request context (trim docs, use retrieve-and-rank to only send relevant chunks). Also consider streaming outputs so you start consuming tokens incrementally (helps in some cases).

kevin_prod: Longer term: you have two options — a) request a quota bump for sustained TPM/RPM (we will need the usage profile + billing tier and this often leads to Dedicated or reserved capacity), b) migrate high-throughput parts of workload to the 32k-quant variant which has lower token cost per request. We also recommend client-side exponential backoff when you see 429s.

sre-bot: Automated note: Investigated token usage spikes for account acme-inc at 2025-11-06T14:12:03Z. Observed tokens/min peak = 4,920,000; policy applied = per_account_per_model_tpm -> throttled; duration 00:00:45.

customer_acme_inc: We tried repro locally: at concurrency 4 it was fine; at 8-12 we got 429s within 30s. So sounds like concurrency cap + TPM both bite. Is there a way to have the platform auto-fallback to a smaller context or a cheaper model when throttling would otherwise happen?

jess_support: Yes — you can configure routing/fallback rules in the Console (Route Policies) to say: prefer rwd-owl-64k but fallback to rwd-owl-32k-quant when tpm usage triggers. Example policy snippet for the Console/routing: 
```json
{
  "route": "customer/acme-inc/generation",
  "primary": "rwd-owl-64k",
  "fallbacks": ["rwd-owl-32k-quant"],
  "fallback_policy": "on_throttle",
  "max_concurrency": 6
}
```

kevin_prod: Also note that edge case: large context = larger latency, which can keep concurrency slots occupied longer, effectively lowering throughput. If latency per request goes from 0.8s -> 6s, concurrency 10 -> throughput drop. So measure average latencies too.

customer_acme_inc: OK that helps. We'll try reducing concurrency and add fallback rules. If we need a sustained increase in TPM what info do you need to request quota bump?

jess_support: Please open a support ticket with: company name, account id, expected sustained RPM and TPM (minute-level and 95th percentile bursts), desired SLA/throughput, and whether PII requires Private/Dedicated. We'll attach the usage logs review and route to the provisioning team. We'll also include recommended immediate config changes in the ticket.

ash_sre: One last tip: if you must keep long contexts, consider chunking client-side and doing an indexed retrieval with relevance scoring so you only send the top ~2-4k tokens per request. That reduces TPM dramatically.

customer_acme_inc: Thanks — saving this convo. Will update ticket with numbers and repro steps. Appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
